name: Modals of deduction: must, might, can't
subtitle: Use must, might and can't to say how sure you are about something. Add have + past participle for the past: She must be tired. He can't have seen us. They might have left.
source: icanspeak English original English text (grammar-b2 run, 2026-10-29)

concept.exampleHtml: She must be tired. — He can't have seen us. — They might have left.

qa.html: How sure are you? Use must when you are almost sure something is true: Amira isn't answering. She must be asleep. Use can't when you are almost sure it is not true: That can't be Tom. He's in Spain. Use might, may or could when it is possible: He might be at the gym. You guess from what you see or know.

About now: modal + infinitive without to. She must be at work. He can't live here. It might be expensive. For something happening now use be + -ing: She must be working. They might be waiting outside.

About the past: modal + have + past participle. She must have left early. They can't have heard us. I might have forgotten my keys. The modal shows how sure you are. have shows that it is about the past. For something that was in progress use have been + -ing: He must have been sleeping.

For a guess, the opposite of must is can't, not mustn't. He must be at home. ↔ He can't be at home. mustn't is for rules: You mustn't be late. In the past, couldn't have also works: He couldn't have known.

Typical mistakes: ✗ He mustn't be at home. His car isn't here. → ✓ He can't be at home. · ✗ She must left early. → ✓ She must have left early. · ✗ They might to be late. → ✓ They might be late. (no to)

concept.noteHtml: might not and can't are not the same. She might not know means it is possible that she does not know. She can't know means you are sure she does not know. In speech, have sounds like 've or of: must've, might've, can't've. Always write have: ✗ must of → ✓ must have. Here the modals are guesses. For ability, permission and rules, see Modal verbs. For plans and predictions, see Future forms.

items: Sure it is true → must: He must be at home.
Sure it is not true → can't: He can't be at home.
might, may, could = possible, not sure
✗ must of left → ✓ must have left

listen.text: She must be tired after the long flight.
listen.note: Almost sure it is true: must + be.

listen.text: He can't be at home. The lights are off.
listen.note: Almost sure it is not true: can't, not mustn't.

listen.text: They might have missed the train.
listen.note: A possibility about the past: might have + past participle.

hoeren.instruction: Listen and choose the words you hear. Listen for must, can't and might.

items.text: They might have missed the bus.
She must have forgotten her phone.
He could be in the garden.

rounds.label: 1 · Now: must or can't
rounds.instruction: You hear a guess. Sure means must. Impossible means can't. Say the sentence with the modal.

items.prompt: Impossible: Tom is at work.
Sure: Priya is at home.
Impossible: this is your bag.
Sure: Kwame is working.
Impossible: they are lost.
Sure: it's expensive.

rounds.label: 2 · The past: must have, can't have, might have
rounds.instruction: You hear a guess about the past. Sure means must have. Impossible means can't have. Maybe means might have.

items.prompt: Impossible: he saw us.
Maybe: they missed the train.
items.answer: They might have missed the train.

items.prompt: Sure: I left my keys at work.
items.answer: I must have left my keys at work.

items.prompt: Impossible: you lost it.
Maybe: Mei took the wrong bus.
items.answer: Mei might have taken the wrong bus.

exercises.title: must, can't or might?
exercises.hint: Is the speaker almost sure it is true (must), almost sure it is not true (can't) or just guessing (might)?
exercises.hintHtml: mustAlmost sure it is true.can'tAlmost sure it is not true.mightPossible, but not sure.

items.prompt: "I saw Tom on the bus!" "That ___ be Tom. He's on holiday in Spain."
items.why: You are sure it is impossible. Use can't, not mustn't.

items.prompt: I'm not sure where Diego is. He ___ be in the garden.
items.why: I'm not sure means it is only possible: might.

items.prompt: The office is empty and Priya's coat has gone. She ___ have left early.
items.why: The evidence is strong, so you are almost sure: must have.

items.prompt: He ___ have seen us. He was 500 metres away and it was dark.
items.why: You are sure it was impossible. Use can't have, not mustn't have.

items.prompt: Mei isn't here yet. She ___ have missed her train, but I'm not sure.
items.why: But I'm not sure means it is only possible: might have.

items.prompt: That ___ be Kwame's phone. His is red, and this one is blue.
items.why: You are sure it is not his phone: can't. Mustn't is for rules.

items.prompt: His car is outside and the lights are on. He ___ be at home.
items.why: The evidence is strong, so you are almost sure: must.

items.prompt: They ___ have gone out. Their coats are still here.
items.why: The coats are the evidence: you are sure they did not go out. Use can't have.

exercises.title: Complete the verb form.
exercises.hint: Now: modal + be (+ -ing). Past: modal + have + past participle. Never use to after a modal.

items.prompt: She isn't answering. She must ___ asleep.
items.why: You are guessing about now: modal + be.

items.prompt: The ground is wet. It must ___ rained in the night.
items.why: The rain is in the past: modal + have + past participle.

items.prompt: They can't have ___ us. The door was closed.
items.why: After have, use the past participle: heard.

items.prompt: You look pale. You must be ___ too hard these days.
items.why: Something happening around now: be + -ing.

items.prompt: She can't ___ forty! She looks twenty-five.
items.why: You are guessing about now: can't + be.

items.prompt: He must have ___ the wrong train. He is still not here.
items.why: After have, use the past participle: taken.

exercises.title: What does it mean?
exercises.hint: must = sure it is true. can't = sure it is not true. might, may, could = possible.

rows.term: She could be in the garden.
I may have lost my keys.

exercises.title: must have, can't have or might have?
exercises.hint: Read the clue. A strong clue gives must have or can't have. Perhaps gives might have.
exercises.hintHtml: must haveA strong clue says it is true.can't haveA strong clue says it is not true.might havePerhaps. It is only possible.

items.prompt: The floor is wet and there is a bucket. Someone ___ cleaned it.
items.why: The wet floor and the bucket are strong clues: must have.

items.prompt: Diego was in Spain all week, so he ___ been at the party.
items.why: He was far away, so it is impossible: can't have.

items.prompt: Liam is late. I'm not sure why. He ___ missed the bus.
items.why: I'm not sure means it is only possible: might have.

items.prompt: She got full marks, so she ___ studied really hard. There is no other way.
items.why: There is no other way means you are sure: must have.

items.prompt: I can hear them laughing and talking, so they ___ gone to bed yet.
items.why: You can hear them, so you are sure they are still up: can't have.

items.prompt: Amira ___ forgotten about the meeting. She wrote it in her diary yesterday.
items.why: She wrote it down yesterday, so you are sure she did not forget: can't have.

exercises.title: What goes together?
exercises.hint: Tap the situation, then the guess that fits it.

pairs.q: The phone is ringing but nobody answers.
pairs.a: They might be in the garden.

pairs.q: She has been awake for 30 hours.
Tom is on holiday in Spain.
pairs.a: That can't be him on the bus.

pairs.q: The window is broken and the door is open.
I can't find my keys anywhere.
pairs.a: I might have left them at work.

pairs.q: Her light is off and her car isn't there.

exercises.title: Gap text: Who ate the cake?
exercises.hint: Is the writer sure it is true, sure it is not true, or just guessing? Also check: now or the past?

segments.text:
Hi Mei,

Someone ate my birthday cake, and I'm trying to find out who. I'm sure it
been one of the team, because nobody else has a key. It
been Tom. He was on holiday all week. It
been Olga, who loves chocolate, but I'm not sure. Now look: there is chocolate on Kwame's desk. He

his chocolate. He is allergic to it.

More soon,
Priya

sentences.hint: almost sure it is true: must + be
almost sure it did not happen: can't have
almost sure about the past: must have been
a possibility, with not: might not
